correctness.rationale: The signature pigeonhole bound rules out all codes of size four or less. The complete predicate equals hitting 16 closed neighborhoods and 120 pairwise symmetric differences. The included finite exhaustive program checks all 1820 size-four and 4368 size-five subsets and confirms the proposed disjoint 16 x 6 templates exactly exhaust the 96 qualifying codes. A separate direct-signature implementation confirms all 96 sets, and the two implementations independently reconstruct and verify exactly 16 six-cycle components with 96 edges. Explicit definitions avoid open/closed and nonempty/allow-empty ambiguity. Finite enumeration is used only to prove the finite claim.

The rook Cartesian-product theorem applies to the nonisomorphic rook graph, not Shrikhande; minimum cardinality of one does not transfer to the other.

value.rationale: The cospectral rook/Shrikhande comparison motivates study of optimal neighborhood-separating sets beyond general strongly regular parameters. Precisely classifying all minimum feasible configurations and proving the sixteen disjoint six-cycle exchange geometry gives a natural sharp connectivity obstruction for optimum-preserving single-sensor relocations; this cannot be inferred from the minimum cardinality or an unrelated metric-basis exchange study. The classification is self-contained and exhaustive on the smallest non-rook (16,6,2,2) strongly regular example.
